summary: The factual content of the sources subject holds up. I re-fetched all 34 URLs (HTTP 200) and re-checked every pin date marker, the 10 repo head SHAs, the blob and path-commit SHAs, and every candidate version, date and license against crates.io, npm, the Go proxy and gh api. The ADR table and pins.json agree on all 34 rows. S07, S22, S27 and the OpenTUI engines (bun >=1.3.0, node >=26.4.0) all match the producer's claims; E1 is accurate in substance but is not a contradiction with the spec sentence. Five problems need fixing before this counts as a trustworthy pin set. (1) The pins are not independently reproducible: 0/34 text hashes can be regenerated, the extraction script is missing, and no snapshots or archive URLs are stored, which falls short of plan line 54 for the 24 non-git sources. (2) The Win32-OpenSSH licence and maintenance statements look at the wrong repository (active code and a LICENCE file are in PowerShell/openssh-portable). (3) The S26 excerpt quotes a sentence that is on S31. (4) The OpenTUI 'node or Bun' and 'via Bun FFI' wording is unlabelled inference. (5) The Pigeons telemetry, root-service and ~/.ssh/config-writing behaviors documented on S19 are missing from the pins and fixture guidance. S17 has also moved since the pin; its quotes still hold and its permalink pin remains valid. My scripts and outputs are in <repo>/tests/evidence/artifacts/review-sources/. That directory also contained earlier files that were already there when I started (fetch_all.py, gh_checks.*, refetch.json); I did not rely on them. Overall verdict: factual claims mostly confirmed, with the major pinning-reproducibility gap and the E6 repository error outstanding. M00-T02 should stay implemented_unverified until those are addressed."
